title: Annotatio VI §.VII: Indigni eat panem Domini (bread of Lord), not panem Dominum (Lord-bread)
pass_a_gloss: And so, for the unworthy’s sake, he introduces only a halved and less principal Object of eating in the legitimate use of the Holy Supper — namely bread alone — writing thus: As often as you eat of this bread and drink of this cup, you will announce the Lord’s death until he return. Whoever therefore eats unworthily of THIS BREAD, he is guilty of Christ’s Body: And thence let a man examine Himself, and so eat of this bread, and drink of this cup. To be sure, this head of Doctrine concerning the Unworthy’s Eating of that bread which is of the Lord, not of that bread which is the Lord himself, much more rightly and evidently than (what the Author wills) the head of doctrine concerning Oral Eating of Christ’s body by the Unworthy.
pass_b_english: For their sake he names only the lesser object — this bread — “whoever eats this bread unworthily is guilty of the body”; examine yourself, then eat and drink.
So the true head is Indigni eating the bread of the Lord, not the bread that is the Lord — clearer than the Author’s Oral-body-of-Indigni head.
source_text: Eóque manducationis, in legitimo S. Cœnæ usu, Objectum dimidiatum duntaxat minusque principale, scilicet panem solum, indignorum causâ, inducit, ita scribens: Quoties de pane hoc ederitis & de poculo hoc biberitis, mortem Domini annuntiabitis, donec redeat. Quicunque igitur indignè de PANE HOC manducat, is reus sit Corporis Christi: Indeque exploret Seipsum homo, & ita edat de pane hoc, & bibat de poculo hoc. Nimirum, hoc Doctrinæ caput de Indignorum Manducatione panis istius, qui Domini est, non autem panis illius, qui Dominus ipse est, rectius ac evidentius multo, quam (quod Auctor vult) caput doctrinæ, de Indignorum Manducatione corporis Christi Orali.

lemmas.latin: panis … qui Domini est … qui Dominus ipse est
lemmas.gloss: bread … of the Lord … which is the Lord himself
